object_entity.proposition_label: Ordination is conferred by the laying on of hands

evidence.notes: Cyprian's conversion narrative presupposes a process of formation before baptism.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: I myself was held in bonds by the innumerable errors of my previous life and did not believe I could be freed from them. But after the stain of former years had been washed away by the aid of the water of new birth, a light from above poured itself upon my heart now cleansed and purified; after the second birth had restored me to a new man by means of the Spirit breathed from heaven, in a marvellous manner what had been doubtful became certain, what had been hidden was revealed.
passage.notes: Cyprian's conversion and baptismal regeneration testimony; Spirit transformation

subject_entity.notes: Rufinus of Aquileia's continuation of Eusebius's Church History in two books (HE 10–11, c. 402); primary Western source for Frumentius and the christianization of Aksum (1.9); covers events from Nicaea to Theodosius I.

object_entity.notes: Historian, theologian, translator; continued Eusebius's Church History in two Latin books (HE 10–11, c. 402); primary Western source for Frumentius and the christianization of Aksum; translated many of Origen's works into Latin.

evidence.notes: HE 1.9 is from Rufinus's own work.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: A philosopher named Meropius of Tyre sailed to India with two boys Frumentius and Aedesius. The ship was seized and all killed except the boys who were brought to the king of Aksum. When the king died the queen asked Frumentius to help govern. Frumentius sought out Roman traders who were Christians and built churches. Later he traveled to Alexandria where Athanasius consecrated him bishop. He returned to Aksum and converted many including the king.
passage.notes: Primary Western source for the christianization of Aksum; Rufinus heard the account from Aedesius himself.
